mechanism: Tesla designs workload-specific inference chips for vehicles, robotics and AI systems; a qualified Terafab process and packaging route could shorten design-to-production cycles, improve supply security and coordinate edge-compute products with SpaceXAI demand, but the public framework is non-binding and discloses no capacity, price, capital or ownership economics.
catalyst: Tesla and SpaceX execute binding Terafab terms; Tesla identifies a qualified chip or package, measurable volume, cost, performance or iteration gains; or Terafab-supported Optimus, autonomy or edge products contribute disclosed economics.
invalidation: The framework does not become definitive; Tesla products remain externally fabricated without an economic disadvantage; Terafab yield, cost or schedule is uncompetitive; related-party terms transfer value; or incremental capex and complexity exceed supply-security and iteration benefits.
